messages.subject: Unusually High MVPA Values
parts:
Hello everyone,


I’m analyzing a dataset of 190 accelerometry recordings from Actigraph accelerometers worn on the wrist, and have noticed unusually high daily values of moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA) when calculated using the sum of bouts_wei for MVPA.


I would greatly appreciate any insights from the group regarding my code—does anything seem off that could be influencing these results? I’ve attached a subset of my accelerometry data along with the script for reference.

The subset consists of three files, which I have uploaded to Google Drive (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1MLUz4oxU7_mOJi_bPi9cwdSxhKleSLzQ?usp=share_link).

Thanks in advance to everyone for your time and support!

Best regards,
Juan Pablo Espinoza

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Unusually High MVPA Values
parts: when calculated using the sum of bouts_wei for MVPA.

Please be more specific about which exact variables from which report you are summing.

I see you are considering bouts of at least 1 minute and work with 5 second epochs resolution, so it is not surprising that you find a lot of time spent in MVPA compared with aggregating to 1 minute, while using an acceleration threshold proposed for adults. So, I do not think the values are surprising.

It also depends on what you are comparing with as being 'normal'. You may want to make sure that your references values were calculated with the similar to your own analysis.

Further:
Chile/Continental => Note that this does not account for day saving time. I would advise using a name that is specific to a city and country in your timezone such as America/Santiago. By doing so GGIR/R takes care of day saving time.

HASPT.algo ="HDZA", => does not exist, "HDCZA" is the correct name.

Vincent

Dr. Vincent van Hees | Independent consultant | https://accelting.com/
